extDescription.message: Flags PHP2Shell-exposed sites, blocks card skimmers, guards passwords, seed phrases, wallet signatures and clipboard. Zero data.

noData.message: Nothing to peek at yet. Reload the page.

notPhp.message: No PHP in sight. Nothing to worry about here.

vulnTitle.message: Advertises a PHP version affected by PHP2Shell

vulnNote.message: The server reports a PHP version older than the fix. Avoid typing passwords or card details and connecting your wallet here until it's patched. This is what the server reports, not proof: some Linux distros patch without changing the version number.

eolTitle.message: Advertises an unsupported PHP version (no PHP2Shell fix)

eolNote.message: The server reports a PHP branch that never got an official fix. Treat it as exposed: no passwords, cards or wallet connections. This is what the server reports, not proof.

hiddenTitle.message: Runs PHP, keeps its version secret

hiddenNote.message: Can't tell from the outside. That's normal — and smart security.

footer.message: No tracking, no data collected, open source. PHPeek only contacts a site when you use “Check any site”.

checkBad.message: That doesn't look like a web address.

patchedNote.message: That's what the server reports, not a guarantee: versions can be hidden or stale. PHPeek's other guards stay on either way.
